clue.text: Managing to get women catching fish

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to be angling

explanation.surface: Someone lands a catch of fish while also getting the company of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' looks like it belongs with the fish but simply joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something is to obtain it by cunning, so wangling is managing to get it by craft.

clue.text: First class call for public discussion

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords with the figure one as a letter I
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A top-quality summons to open debate.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is old slang for first-rate; setters often write the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a topic an airing means exposing it to open debate.

clue.text: Departed with ring-leader, being beyond help

parts.note: departed means gone, left or died

indicators.note: a leader is the front of something, so the word ring gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone has fled with the gang boss and is a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-leader' reads as one word, the head of a gang, but it is split: the leader of 'ring'. 'being' is a noun in the definition, a creature beyond help.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is a person or thing that is doomed or past saving.

clue.text: Pony club first had this old engine

indicators.note: first tells us the club comes before the pony in the answer

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A riding club once owned this antique locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pony club' looks like a riding club for children, but the words split: the club (a golf iron) goes first, then the pony as a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse was the nineteenth-century nickname for a steam locomotive.

clue.text: Looked happy about new church

indicators.note: about means the happy word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: happy means glad
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone looked pleased with the new church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy about' reads as pleased with something, but 'about' is a container signal wrapping the happy word around the new church.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look quickly, so glanced is a past-tense synonym of looked.

clue.text: Face when soundly kissed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word for kissed is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: pecked means kissed lightly

explanation.surface: A face pictured at the moment of being thoroughly kissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals a homophone: PECKED said aloud gives the ending PECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one side or facet of a matter, as in a different face of the problem.

clue.text: A very soft semi-pale fruit

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

indicators.note: semi means half, here the second half of the word pale

explanation.surface: A squashy, pale-looking piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In music PP stands for pianissimo, very soft.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Little weight attached to argument in favour of broadcast

indicators.note: attached to puts the weight after the argument in the answer

parts.note: a pro is a point in favour, as in pros and cons
a gramme is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A small detail added to the case in support of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'argument in favour of' is a noun here, a point for the case; 'attached to' puts the little weight after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a show that is broadcast on radio or television.

clue.text: The president's valet supports a rocker, for example

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'the president is'

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a rocker, a rocking chair, is an example of a chair
a man is a manservant or valet

explanation.surface: The head of state's manservant holds up a fan of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rocker' suggests a rock musician but is a rocking chair. In a down clue 'supports' puts MAN underneath CHAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a meeting or company, acting as its president.

clue.text: Smile, and leave an American in Mexico

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone smiles and walks out on an American while in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringo is the Latin American term for a foreigner, especially a North American.

clue.text: Demonstrate the truth, mostly, in a friend's blessing

indicators.note: in places the shortened proof inside the friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for demonstrate

parts.note: to prove is to demonstrate the truth of something

explanation.surface: Showing honesty earns most of a friend's blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter off the word for demonstrating the truth, and 'in' puts what is left inside the friend, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval and blessing both mean consent or endorsement.

clue.text: Can a rich display be out of control?

indicators.note: display means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Can a wealthy show turn into chaos?
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges the letters of CAN A RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes a state with no order or rule, so it is chaotic.

clue.text: Faults caused by fears without their leader

indicators.note: without their leader means the word for fears loses its first letter

parts.note: terrors are great fears

explanation.surface: Mistakes made because of anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without their leader' drops the T from TERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes or faults.

clue.text: Both comrades fell, unable to continue

indicators.note: fell suggests the letters have tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Two comrades fall in battle and can fight no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' rearranges BOTH COMRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hors de combat is French for out of the fight, now used of anyone disabled from carrying on.

clue.text: Chess? Try one move that gives a panic attack

indicators.note: move suggests the letters change position

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A chess player tries one move and has a fit of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges CHESS, TRY and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics are a fit of wild uncontrolled emotion, like a bout of panic.

clue.text: Standard set by London theatre

explanation.surface: A benchmark established by a West End playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Criterion is a theatre on Piccadilly Circus in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard for judging, and the Criterion is also a famous London playhouse.

clue.text: Posed with union leader — the charge is steep

parts.note: a model who posed sat for the artist

indicators.note: leader means only the opening letter of union is used

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A model sits with a trade union boss and the fee is very high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for a price, but it is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it completely in liquid.

clue.text: Zeal arises if given no interference

indicators.note: given here means the letters are yielded up in a fresh form

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm grows when people are left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' rearranges the letters of ZEAL ARISES IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Laissez-faire is the French phrase for a policy of letting things take their own course without intervening.

clue.text: Bill languishes outside, making deceptive appearances

indicators.note: outside puts the word for languishes around the bill

parts.note: fades means weakens or languishes
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A notice drooping on an outer wall gives a false impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is a common word for an account, not a name; 'outside' wraps the languishing word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is a false front put on to deceive, so the plural means misleading shows.

clue.text: Bar the audience?

parts.note: the word for the audience at large is also the word that comes before bar in a pub's main saloon

explanation.surface: Should the spectators be kept out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a verb meaning exclude, but it points to the public bar of a pub; the audience is the general public.
explanation.definitionFit: The general population is the public, and a pub's plainer room is the public bar.

clue.text: Marvellous — drink starts everyone rambling benignly

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: starts means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A great drink sets everyone chattering kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes E, R and B from the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Went to pieces, being without money

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed after running out of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is the past of break, to shatter, and also slang for having no money.

clue.text: Vet pays for goods here

explanation.surface: An animal doctor settles the bill at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor but is the verb, to check out.
explanation.definitionFit: To check out is to examine or vet, and a checkout is the shop till where purchases are paid for.

clue.text: Cutter lifted from reef in Korea

indicators.note: lifted says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blade raised from a reef off the Korean coast.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lifted' reads the run E F I N K upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a blade used to cut things.

clue.text: Crew provided antique with many uses

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
if means provided that
antique means old

explanation.surface: Sailors given a versatile old object.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and varied, so a thing with many purposes.

clue.text: Freezing point

parts.note: read not as a temperature but as a frozen spike that tapers to a tip

explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of frozen water with a sharp tip.

clue.text: The French understand a tenant

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: The French grasp what a renter is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, as a tenant does.

clue.text: Pronounce judgement on language construction

explanation.surface: A judge rules on a point of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence is to pass judgement on a convict, and a sentence is a grammatical unit of words.
